findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff renumbers a published process-boundary exit code: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changes from 4 to 3 and the value 4 is repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, with no consumer-migration note. Any wrapper script or CI job written against the previously shipped preview behavior of 'kc.sh update-compatibility' that branched on exit code 4 (recreate required) will now silently interpret a recreate-required run (exit 3) as an unknown/other failure, and a feature-disabled run (exit 4) as 'recreate required' — inverted semantics with no error at the call site. Author rebuttal is 'it is preview and now matches the documented table', which mitigates but does not remove the breakage for early adopters of the shipped preview command.

[ADVISORY] The feature key 'rolling-updates' is hand-duplicated across at least five unconnected sites in this diff (printFeatureDisabled message here, the kc.adoc template macro, two doc guides, Dockerfile-custom-image, and the UpdateCommandDistTest ENABLE_FEATURE constant) while the gating code alone uses Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES, with no single source of truth. If the feature key is ever renamed or the feature graduates (flag removed/no longer required), the compiler catches only the enum-based check; the error message, both doc guides, the command template macro, the Dockerfile build line, and the test constant all silently go stale, producing documentation that instructs users to pass an invalid --features value and an error message that names a nonexistent feature. The next change gets riskier because five string sites must be found manually.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never asserts the new CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4) exit code, and the feature-disabled path of the 'check' subcommand is not exercised by any test in this diff at all (only 'metadata'). A regression that changes the disabled-path exit code (e.g. picocli falling back to exit code 1, or the check silently proceeding instead of exiting 4) passes CI, so external consumers keying on exit code 4 per the newly documented table in update-compatibility.adoc get wrong results with no test failure to warn the maintainer.

[BUG] The new testFeatureNotEnabled test asserts only the error message and never asserts the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4), leaving the new exit-code contract added in this diff completely unverified. CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 and the docs table row 'm|4' in update-compatibility.adoc promise exit code 4 when the feature is off; nothing pins that value. A regression that returns e.g. picocli's USAGE=2 (or 0) instead of 4 would pass this test while breaking every script that branches on the documented exit code — the exact class of consumer this constant exists for. testCompatible already demonstrates the pattern (assertEquals(0, result.exitCode()) via distribution.run), so verifying the 4 is feasible with the existing harness; the sibling testWrongVersions likewise asserts only messages, so the renumbered RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE=3 is also unpinned.

[BUG] createInitialDeployment now unconditionally enables ROLLING_UPDATES for every strategy, so the operator's documented failure mode when the feature is disabled — the very CAUTION added in advanced-configuration.adoc ('Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail') — has no test coverage in this diff. The docs added in this PR promise a hard operator failure for deployments that lack spec.features.enabled=[rolling-updates]; no test in the diff exercises that path (UpgradeTest always sets FeatureSpec.setEnabledFeatures, and UpdateCommandDistTest only covers the CLI commands). If the gating the docs promise silently regresses or never fires on the operator path (e.g. the operator invokes update-compatibility without forwarding the CR's features), users with an existing update.strategy would get a silently wrong upgrade behavior instead of the documented failure, and no test would catch it.

[ADVISORY] The feature-gate block (isFeatureEnabled check + printFeatureDisabled + picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) + return) is duplicated verbatim in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() instead of being hoisted into AbstractUpdatesCommand alongside printFeatureDisabled(). The next change to the gating (a second gated feature, a different exit code, a reordered check against validateConfig) must be applied in two places; if one is missed the two subcommands of the same update-compatibility command disagree on whether the feature is enabled — an inconsistency invisible to the current tests, which cover the disabled path only via the metadata subcommand (testFeatureNotEnabled) and never cross-check check-vs-metadata parity.

[ADVISORY] Dockerfile-custom-image hardcodes --features=rolling-updates into the build, force-enabling a preview feature for every image built from this template regardless of whether the consumer uses rolling updates. Anyone using operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image as the documented way to build a custom Keycloak image (e.g. to add providers) gets the preview ROLLING_UPDATES feature silently enabled in their production image, inheriting preview-stage behavior and the associated operator upgrade gating without ever opting in; the flag should be a build ARG defaulting to off, not a hardcoded value.

[ADVISORY] The diff silently renumbers the public exit-code contract (RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE 4→3, FEATURE_DISABLED=4) inside a PR whose stated intent is only adding a feature flag, with no migration note or operator-side counterpart in the diff. Any consumer scripted against the old contract — including the Keycloak Operator, which invokes this CLI and classifies results by exit code — misclassifies outcomes during version skew: an operator built against the old constant maps the new FEATURE_DISABLED (4) to 'recreate upgrade required' and takes the deployment down instead of failing fast on the missing preview feature, and scripts keying on exit 4 for 'recreate' now silently break. This untraceable contract change deserves its own changelog entry and coordinated operator handling.

[ADVISORY] The user-facing custom-image Dockerfile template now hardcodes --features=rolling-updates into the image build, enabling a preview feature for every image built from this template regardless of whether the deployment uses rolling updates. Users who copy this template for ordinary custom-image builds (custom themes/providers, unrelated configuration) get a preview feature implicitly enabled; when the feature's semantics change (it is PREVIEW and 'may change or be removed'), or when they later upgrade, their builds and server behavior drift from what they configured, and removing the flag becomes a required edit in a file they may not associate with update behavior. The CR-level FeatureSpec shown in the docs and tests is the intended enablement path; baking it into the build template is test convenience leaking into shipped operator tooling.

[ADVISORY] The feature gate is duplicated per-subcommand (identical check in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run, plus printFeatureDisabled in AbstractUpdatesCommand) instead of being enforced once in the shared base class or the parent UpdateCompatibility command. The next subcommand added to the update-compatibility group (or a refactor that adds a code path before run(), e.g. argument validation that performs work) silently lacks the gate, so the 'feature must be enabled' invariant is only enforced on the two commands that happen to have the copy-pasted block today; the error text and exit path must then be kept in sync in N+1 places.

[ADVISORY] The new disabled-feature test asserts only the error message and never asserts the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4) that downstream consumers — the Operator and user scripts — depend on after the RECREATE renumbering. If the exit code value drifts again (e.g. a future renumber or collision with picocli's USAGE=2), every test in this diff still passes while the operator's classification of 'feature disabled' silently breaks; the exit code is the entire cross-process contract introduced by this PR and it has zero test coverage.

[ADVISORY] The docs assert unconditionally that 'the Operator will fail' without the feature, but the diff contains no operator-side enforcement — the only gate added is inside the two server CLI commands — and UpgradeTest enables the feature for every strategy, so the claimed failure path is never exercised. Users running strategy: Recreate (the documented default alternative in this very section) are told the operator fails without the feature; if enforcement actually only triggers via the update-compatibility exit code on the rolling path (or vice versa), users enable a preview feature they don't need, or hit an undocumented failure mode, and no test in this diff can distinguish which claim is true.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3 while its old value 4 is reassigned to the new FEATURE_DISABLED result, flipping the meaning of exit code 4 from 'recreate upgrade required' to 'command refused, feature disabled' with no version bump of the CLI's machine-readable contract. Existing automation that keys on exit code 4 to mean 'recreate needed, schedule downtime' now receives 4 for a run that was merely refused because a preview flag is off, and receives 3 for an actual recreate verdict; scripts that branch on 3 as a generic error will misroute a genuine recreate-required result, and no caller can distinguish 'assessment says recreate' from 'tool refused to run' without parsing stderr.

[BUG] picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) is not valid Java: 'picocli' is a package, not a class, variable, or statically-imported symbol in this file (the added imports are Profile and CompatibilityResult only), so the expression cannot resolve and the module does not compile. The build fails; the intended call is CommandLine.exit(...) using the already-imported picocli.CommandLine (or a static import of CommandLine.exit), and the same defect is duplicated in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java lines 46-50.

[BUG] Same non-resolvable call picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) as in UpdateCompatibilityCheck: 'picocli' is a package qualifier, not an expression, so this line cannot compile with the imports this diff adds. Build failure of the quarkus runtime module; needs CommandLine.exit(...) or an explicit static import of picocli.CommandLine.exit.

[ADVISORY] The new test asserts only the stderr message for the feature-disabled path and never asserts exit code 4, and it exercises only the Metadata subcommand, leaving both the FEATURE_DISABLED exit-code contract and the identical gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck uncovered. A regression that changes the exit code (e.g. collides with the relocated RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE=3, or a future edit renumbering the constants) ships green because the message still matches; the exit code is precisely the surface external automation consumes and the only part of this change with no coverage.

[ADVISORY] The literal string '--features=rolling-updates' is hand-duplicated across the kc.adoc template macro, operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image line 5, and the test constant in UpdateCommandDistTest instead of deriving from Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey(), creating five independent copies of the feature key with no single source of truth. When the feature is renamed, graduated out of preview (the gate and flag become dead code to remove), or its key casing changes, each copy must be found and updated manually; a missed copy yields documentation or a custom operator image whose build instructs users to pass a flag that no longer exists, failing with 'feature not enabled'.

[ADVISORY] The added CAUTION block states unconditionally that 'the {project_name} Operator will fail' without the rolling-updates feature, and the modified example applies it to the Recreate strategy, which existing deployments already use today without any feature flag. Per this documentation, every existing operator user who has already set update.strategy (including the pre-existing, non-preview Recreate value) must enable a preview feature on their production CR after upgrading or the operator fails; if the operator gate is actually scoped to Rolling only, the doc overstates the requirement and drives users to enable an unstable preview flag unnecessarily — either way the doc and the (out-of-diff) operator gate disagree about the boundary of the feature's blast radius.

[ADVISORY] Gating the read-only compatibility-assessment commands behind the ROLLING_UPDATES capability flag conflates 'assess whether a rolling upgrade is possible' with 'perform a rolling update', and the gate block is copy-pasted identically into UpdateCompatibilityMetadata instead of being extracted to AbstractUpdatesCommand. An operator who wants to plan an upgrade (the tool's entire purpose) must first enable a preview feature on the deployment config, so the planning path is unavailable to anyone following the not-in-production policy for preview features; and when the feature graduates, the duplicated 4-line gate must be removed from each command class individually, with the next added updates command copying it a third time.

[ADVISORY] The published exit-code contract of the update-compatibility tool is silently renumbered: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changes from 4 to 3 and the value 4 is repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, without any migration note or changelog entry in this diff. Existing automation (CI jobs, upgrade runbooks, operator wrappers) that branches on exit code 4 meaning 'shut down and recreate' now receives 4 only when the feature flag is missing and 3 for a genuine recreate requirement; a script following the previously documented contract will shut down a deployment that merely needs `--features=rolling-updates` added, and will treat a real recreate-required result (3) as an unknown/soft failure. Whoever consumes this tool's exit codes gets silently inverted semantics on upgrade.

[ADVISORY] The hard feature gate breaks every pre-existing invocation of the update-compatibility commands: code that previously ran unconditionally now exits 4 with an error whenever the new preview flag is absent, and only in-tree callers (tests, docs template, operator Dockerfile) were retrofitted with the flag. Out-of-tree consumers — user upgrade scripts, CI pipelines, and any operator-side or external tooling that shells out to `kc.sh update-compatibility` from the previous release — stop working outright on upgrade, failing with exit 4 'feature not enabled' until someone discovers the flag in the docs. A PR nominally 'adding a feature flag' silently disables an existing (preview) command for all current users; this objective change should be an explicitly accepted decision, not a side effect.

[ADVISORY] The shared updatecompatibility doc macro hardcodes `--features=rolling-updates` into every documented invocation, changing the command rendered by all includes of this template rather than only the update-compatibility guide. Any other guide or page that includes this macro now instructs readers to enable the preview rolling-updates feature even where the surrounding text never mentions it, coupling unrelated documentation to this feature's preview lifecycle; when the feature graduates or is renamed, every rendered doc page using the macro breaks at once, and users who already pass their own `--features=...` list get a second, conflicting `--features` argument in the copied command.

[ADVISORY] The custom-image build recipe bakes `--features=rolling-updates` unconditionally into every image built from it, enabling a preview feature at image-build time independent of the deployment's declared intent. Anyone using this recipe as the template for their production custom Keycloak images gets the preview rolling-updates feature silently enabled in all derived images, including images used for non-rolling deployments; the feature's enabled/disabled state is now fixed at build time rather than controlled per-deployment via the CR `features` field this same PR documents, so the two configuration paths the PR introduces can disagree.

[ADVISORY] The feature-disabled guard (check + printFeatureDisabled + picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) + return) is hand-duplicated across UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata instead of being enforced once in the shared AbstractUpdatesCommand run path, and the parent UpdateCompatibility command itself carries no gate. The next command added to this family must remember to re-copy the guard or it silently bypasses the feature gate (the exact drift the guard exists to prevent); a future change to the exit code or error message — already shown to be volatile by this diff renumbering the codes — must be edited in N+1 places, and the message string 'rolling-updates' is duplicated as a literal in both copies and the test on top of the enum key.

[ADVISORY] The diff reassigns the documented exit-code contract: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changes from 4 to 3 while the freed code 4 is repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, so any external automation pinned to these codes now conflates 'feature disabled' with 'recreate upgrade required'. Scripts, CI jobs, or operator automation written against the previous contract (exit 4 = recreate required, anything else = compatible/failure) will, on encountering the new FEATURE_DISABLED=4, take the recreate-required branch and shut down or recreate a healthy deployment, and will encounter the new recreate code 3 as an unknown error with no documented meaning; the change is verbatim in the diff (`int RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 4;` → `int RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 3; int FEATURE_DISABLED = 4;`) with no version note, changelog entry, or migration guidance anywhere in the diff, and the operator documentation added in this same diff does not document any exit codes, so operators discover the new contract only by failure.

[BUG] testMissingOptionOnSave was moved onto the feature-enabled path (ENABLE_FEATURE added to @Launch) but its only assertion is the negative `cliResult.assertNoMessage("Missing required argument")`, so it passes identically whether the feature was actually applied or the new gate in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() fired and short-circuited the command. If a regression makes the gate fire despite --features=rolling-updates (or the flag is silently ignored on this subcommand path), this test still passes, giving false confidence that the enabled-path option handling was exercised; nothing in the test positively verifies the metadata command reached its validation logic (no assertMessage of the preview warning, no exit-code check).

[ADVISORY] The new feature gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() is never triggered by any test in the diff: the only feature-disabled test (testFeatureNotEnabled) launches {UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME} and exercises only the metadata command's gate. A regression in the check command's gate (wrong message, wrong exit code, missing early return so the check runs anyway) ships undetected; the checked test file UpdateCommandDistTest.java contains no launch of UpdateCompatibilityCheck.NAME without ENABLE_FEATURE.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message text and never asserts the exit code 4 that picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) produces — the very contract the diff documents in update-compatibility.adoc's new table row 'm|4'. Scripts and automation (including the operator-facing workflows this feature targets) branch on exit codes; a regression that keeps the message but returns 0 or 3 would pass this test while breaking every consumer that dispatches on the documented code 4.

[ADVISORY] testWrongVersions exercises the recreate path (incompatible versions -> 'Rolling Upgrade is not available') but asserts no exit code, so the behavioral change of RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 in CompatibilityResult.java is verified by no test in the diff. Any regression that reverts the constant to 4 (now colliding with FEATURE_DISABLED) or returns a different code on the recreate path passes the suite while silently changing the public CLI contract that external automation and the documented table row 'm|3' depend on.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds the documented claim that the Operator 'will fail' when rolling-updates is not enabled (advanced-configuration.adoc CAUTION block), but the only operator test change (createInitialDeployment) unconditionally enables the feature via FeatureSpec, and no test in the diff deploys an update strategy without it. The operator-side gating failure mode announced to users in this diff's docs is unverified: a regression that lets the operator proceed silently without the feature, or fails with an unusable error, passes the suite; scanned test files: UpgradeTest.java (the only operator test modified) references ROLLING_UPDATES only in createInitialDeployment's enabled path.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changes from 4 to 3 while 4 is repurposed for FEATURE_DISABLED, breaking the shipped exit-code contract that existing automation and the previous docs table rely on (4 = recreate required). Scripts/CI pipelines written against the previous release's contract that branch on exit code 4 ('shut down and recreate') will instead see 3 for a required-recreate result — an unhandled code they may treat as success and attempt a rolling upgrade across incompatible versions, risking split-brain/cache corruption mid-upgrade — while an exit of 4 (feature now disabled) triggers an unnecessary full-deployment shutdown. The change is invisible to out-of-tree consumers because no migration note or versioned exit-code mapping accompanies it.

[ADVISORY] FEATURE_DISABLED (4) reuses the exact exit code that the previous release shipped for RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE (4), while RECREATE moves to 3, so any consumer built against the released behavior misclassifies the feature-disabled exit as a 'recreate required' verdict. A script or older operator integration that ran the pre-gate `update-compatibility check` and treated exit 4 as 'the deployment must be shut down before applying the new configuration' now receives 4 whenever the preview feature is left at its default (disabled) — the compatibility check never ran at all, yet the consumer acts on it as if the check had determined a recreate is required, triggering an unnecessary full shutdown/recreate instead of either an error or a valid rolling-upgrade verdict; symmetrically, recreate verdicts that previously surfaced as 4 now arrive as 3 and land in any legacy 'unknown exit code' branch. The deliberate renumbering is documented in the comment, but the collision with the shipped value has no migration note.

[ADVISORY] The feature gate is a copy-pasted 5-line block duplicated in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() instead of a single guard in AbstractUpdatesCommand, so the gate's coverage depends on each subcommand author remembering to paste it. The next subcommand added to UpdateCompatibility (or a refactor that reorders one of these run() methods) silently bypasses the gate and executes preview compatibility logic with the feature disabled — exactly the unguarded-execution state the docs caution causes the Operator to fail — with no compile-time or structural signal that the gate was omitted. A shared guard in AbstractUpdatesCommand.run() (or a picocli-ordering hook) would make the omission impossible rather than remembered.

[ADVISORY] The new caution states unqualified that 'the {project_name} Operator will fail' when the rolling-updates feature is not enabled, implying the gate applies to all update strategies including Recreate, and the updated UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment indeed sets the feature unconditionally for both Recreate and Rolling strategies. If the operator enforces the gate regardless of strategy (as the unqualified doc wording and the strategy-agnostic test setup indicate), every existing deployment running `strategy: Recreate` — which never needed a compatibility check — starts failing reconciliation after upgrading to this operator version unless the user hand-edits the CR to enable a preview feature; if the gate is actually scoped to rolling updates only, the caution overstates the failure and misdirects Recreate users into enabling an unnecessary preview feature. Either way the doc as written does not tell Recreate users what actually happens to them.

That means the operator integration upgrade test no longer exercises (and cannot catch regressions in) the “feature disabled” scenario that the docs added as a hard failure condition (`advanced-configuration.adoc` CAUTION about operator failing if `rolling-updates` not enabled). adjudication.rationale: The diff adds the same feature-gating block in both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` (`if (!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)) { printFeatureDisabled(); picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED); return; }`), while only `printFeatureDisabled()` is centralized in `AbstractUpdatesCommand`. The tests also only assert the disabled-feature behavior through launching `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` (`testFeatureNotEnabled`), and all test paths involving `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` pass `--features=rolling-updates`, so parity between `check` and `metadata` for the disabled path is not covered by the current diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Dockerfile-custom-image hardcodes --features=rolling-updates into the build, force-enabling a preview feature for every image built from this template regardless of whether the consumer uses rolling updates. Anyone using operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image as the documented way to build a custom Keycloak image (e.g. to add providers) gets the preview ROLLING_UPDATES feature silently enabled in their production image, inheriting preview-stage behavior and the associated operator upgrade gating without ever opting in; the flag should be a build ARG defaulting to off, not a hardcoded value.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly hardcodes `--features=rolling-updates` into `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image` (`RUN /opt/keycloak/bin/kc.sh build ... --features=rolling-updates`). Since `ROLLING_UPDATES` is introduced as a PREVIEW feature and the docs added in this PR state it must be enabled or operator/commands fail, baking it into the template makes every custom image built from this template opt into that preview feature by default. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded concern about default behavior/opt-in rather than a clearly verifiable functional defect (it may be intentional to keep the operator working).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff silently renumbers the public exit-code contract (RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE 4→3, FEATURE_DISABLED=4) inside a PR whose stated intent is only adding a feature flag, with no migration note or operator-side counterpart in the diff. Any consumer scripted against the old contract — including the Keycloak Operator, which invokes this CLI and classifies results by exit code — misclassifies outcomes during version skew: an operator built against the old constant maps the new FEATURE_DISABLED (4) to 'recreate upgrade required' and takes the deployment down instead of failing fast on the missing preview feature, and scripts keying on exit 4 for 'recreate' now silently break. This untraceable contract change deserves its own changelog entry and coordinated operator handling.

[ADVISORY] The user-facing custom-image Dockerfile template now hardcodes --features=rolling-updates into the image build, enabling a preview feature for every image built from this template regardless of whether the deployment uses rolling updates. Users who copy this template for ordinary custom-image builds (custom themes/providers, unrelated configuration) get a preview feature implicitly enabled; when the feature's semantics change (it is PREVIEW and 'may change or be removed'), or when they later upgrade, their builds and server behavior drift from what they configured, and removing the flag becomes a required edit in a file they may not associate with update behavior. The CR-level FeatureSpec shown in the docs and tests is the intended enablement path; baking it into the build template is test convenience leaking into shipped operator tooling.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does hardcode the preview feature into the shipped custom-image template: `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image` changes `kc.sh build ...` to include `--features=rolling-updates`. That means anyone copying this template will build images with the preview feature enabled regardless of whether they intended to use rolling updates, which is a real UX/maintenance concern (feature drift when preview semantics change). This is not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone (it may be intentional given the new docs/CLI gating), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded review issue about how/where feature enablement is applied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The feature gate is duplicated per-subcommand (identical check in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run, plus printFeatureDisabled in AbstractUpdatesCommand) instead of being enforced once in the shared base class or the parent UpdateCompatibility command. The next subcommand added to the update-compatibility group (or a refactor that adds a code path before run(), e.g. argument validation that performs work) silently lacks the gate, so the 'feature must be enabled' invariant is only enforced on the two commands that happen to have the copy-pasted block today; the error text and exit path must then be kept in sync in N+1 places.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the same feature-gate logic duplicated in two subcommands: both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` start with `if (!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)) { printFeatureDisabled(); picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED); return; }`. `AbstractUpdatesCommand` only adds `printFeatureDisabled()` but does not enforce the gate centrally, so any new/update-compatibility subcommand added later could omit the guard unless the developer remembers to copy it again. This is a maintainability/architecture issue grounded in the shown code, not an immediate functional defect in the current diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new disabled-feature test asserts only the error message and never asserts the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4) that downstream consumers — the Operator and user scripts — depend on after the RECREATE renumbering. If the exit code value drifts again (e.g. a future renumber or collision with picocli's USAGE=2), every test in this diff still passes while the operator's classification of 'feature disabled' silently breaks; the exit code is the entire cross-process contract introduced by this PR and it has zero test coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In `UpdateCommandDistTest`, the newly added `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error message (`cliResult.assertError(...)`) and does not assert the process exit code. This matters because the diff explicitly introduces a new cross-process contract via `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (and renumbers `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3) and the CLI commands call `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is disabled. Without an exit-code assertion, a future drift/collision in exit codes could break operator/user-script behavior without any test failing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The docs assert unconditionally that 'the Operator will fail' without the feature, but the diff contains no operator-side enforcement — the only gate added is inside the two server CLI commands — and UpgradeTest enables the feature for every strategy, so the claimed failure path is never exercised. Users running strategy: Recreate (the documented default alternative in this very section) are told the operator fails without the feature; if enforcement actually only triggers via the update-compatibility exit code on the rolling path (or vice versa), users enable a preview feature they don't need, or hit an undocumented failure mode, and no test in this diff can distinguish which claim is true.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds documentation CAUTION blocks stating the Operator/commands will fail unless `rolling-updates` is enabled (docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc, docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc). In code, the only explicit enforcement shown is in the server CLI commands UpdateCompatibilityCheck/Metadata, which now exit with FEATURE_DISABLED if the profile feature isn’t enabled. No operator runtime enforcement change is shown in this diff (only operator test setup changes and a Dockerfile build flag), and UpgradeTest unconditionally enables the feature via FeatureSpec, so the “feature disabled” path is not exercised there. This makes the doc claim potentially misleading relative to what this diff demonstrably enforces, and highlights a concrete gap in coverage/validation for the operator-side behavior implied by the docs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3 while its old value 4 is reassigned to the new FEATURE_DISABLED result, flipping the meaning of exit code 4 from 'recreate upgrade required' to 'command refused, feature disabled' with no version bump of the CLI's machine-readable contract. Existing automation that keys on exit code 4 to mean 'recreate needed, schedule downtime' now receives 4 for a run that was merely refused because a preview flag is off, and receives 3 for an actual recreate verdict; scripts that branch on 3 as a generic error will misroute a genuine recreate-required result, and no caller can distinguish 'assessment says recreate' from 'tool refused to run' without parsing stderr.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (quarkus/runtime/.../CompatibilityResult.java). Additionally, the update-compatibility commands now `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when the `rolling-updates` preview feature is not enabled (UpdateCompatibilityCheck/Metadata). This flips the meaning of exit code 4 from “recreate upgrade required” to “feature disabled/refused to run,” which is a breaking change to the CLI’s machine-readable exit-code contract without any indication in the diff of a compatibility/versioning strategy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) is not valid Java: 'picocli' is a package, not a class, variable, or statically-imported symbol in this file (the added imports are Profile and CompatibilityResult only), so the expression cannot resolve and the module does not compile. The build fails; the intended call is CommandLine.exit(...) using the already-imported picocli.CommandLine (or a static import of CommandLine.exit), and the same defect is duplicated in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java lines 46-50.

adjudication.rationale: In both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`, the diff adds `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED);` while only importing `picocli.CommandLine` (not a `picocli` class/variable nor a static import of `CommandLine.exit`). In Java, a package name (`picocli`) cannot be used as an expression receiver, so `picocli.exit(...)` will not resolve and will fail compilation. The intended call would be `CommandLine.exit(...)` (or a static import).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Same non-resolvable call picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) as in UpdateCompatibilityCheck: 'picocli' is a package qualifier, not an expression, so this line cannot compile with the imports this diff adds. Build failure of the quarkus runtime module; needs CommandLine.exit(...) or an explicit static import of picocli.CommandLine.exit.

adjudication.rationale: In both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`, the diff adds `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED);` while only importing `picocli.CommandLine`. In Java, `picocli` is a package name, not an expression, so `picocli.exit(...)` cannot resolve/compile. It should be `CommandLine.exit(...)` (or a static import of `CommandLine.exit`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new test asserts only the stderr message for the feature-disabled path and never asserts exit code 4, and it exercises only the Metadata subcommand, leaving both the FEATURE_DISABLED exit-code contract and the identical gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck uncovered. A regression that changes the exit code (e.g. collides with the relocated RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE=3, or a future edit renumbering the constants) ships green because the message still matches; the exit code is precisely the surface external automation consumes and the only part of this change with no coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In `UpdateCommandDistTest`, the new `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the stderr text and does not assert the exit code, even though both `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` now call `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` (new constant `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` in `CompatibilityResult`). The test also only launches `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` (not `UpdateCompatibilityCheck`) in the feature-disabled scenario, so the identical gate in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` is not covered. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test/contract-coverage issue rather than a functional bug in the implementation shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The literal string '--features=rolling-updates' is hand-duplicated across the kc.adoc template macro, operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image line 5, and the test constant in UpdateCommandDistTest instead of deriving from Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey(), creating five independent copies of the feature key with no single source of truth. When the feature is renamed, graduated out of preview (the gate and flag become dead code to remove), or its key casing changes, each copy must be found and updated manually; a missed copy yields documentation or a custom operator image whose build instructs users to pass a flag that no longer exists, failing with 'feature not enabled'.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple hard-coded occurrences of the feature flag string, e.g. `--features=rolling-updates` in `docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc`, `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image`, and the test constant `ENABLE_FEATURE = "--features=rolling-updates"` in `UpdateCommandDistTest`. Separately, the key `rolling-updates` is also duplicated in docs and in code via `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()` (e.g. `UpgradeTest`). This is a maintainability concern: if the feature key changes, these literals won’t automatically follow `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()`. It’s not a functional bug shown by the diff today, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The added CAUTION block states unconditionally that 'the {project_name} Operator will fail' without the rolling-updates feature, and the modified example applies it to the Recreate strategy, which existing deployments already use today without any feature flag. Per this documentation, every existing operator user who has already set update.strategy (including the pre-existing, non-preview Recreate value) must enable a preview feature on their production CR after upgrading or the operator fails; if the operator gate is actually scoped to Rolling only, the doc overstates the requirement and drives users to enable an unstable preview flag unnecessarily — either way the doc and the (out-of-diff) operator gate disagree about the boundary of the feature's blast radius.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an unconditional CAUTION in the operator guide: “feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.” and updates the example to enable `rolling-updates` even when `update.strategy` is `Recreate|<not set>`. That documentation change broadens the apparent requirement beyond “Rolling Updates” and could push users to enable a preview feature unnecessarily. However, this PR diff does not show any operator-side gating/failure logic tied to `ROLLING_UPDATES`, so the claim about a doc/operator boundary mismatch can’t be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Gating the read-only compatibility-assessment commands behind the ROLLING_UPDATES capability flag conflates 'assess whether a rolling upgrade is possible' with 'perform a rolling update', and the gate block is copy-pasted identically into UpdateCompatibilityMetadata instead of being extracted to AbstractUpdatesCommand. An operator who wants to plan an upgrade (the tool's entire purpose) must first enable a preview feature on the deployment config, so the planning path is unavailable to anyone following the not-in-production policy for preview features; and when the feature graduates, the duplicated 4-line gate must be removed from each command class individually, with the next added updates command copying it a third time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a hard gate in both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` requiring `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)`; otherwise they print an error and exit with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (new constant). This is a real, diff-grounded design/UX concern: the read-only compatibility/planning commands now fail unless the preview feature is enabled (also documented in the added CAUTION blocks and enforced in `kc.adoc` by appending `--features=rolling-updates`). The finding’s point about duplicated gating logic is also grounded: the same 4-line check is copy-pasted into both command classes rather than being centralized (only `printFeatureDisabled()` was added to `AbstractUpdatesCommand`, not the gate itself). This is not a verifiable correctness defect because the behavior is intentional per docs/tests, but it is a specific maintainability/architecture issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The published exit-code contract of the update-compatibility tool is silently renumbered: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changes from 4 to 3 and the value 4 is repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, without any migration note or changelog entry in this diff. Existing automation (CI jobs, upgrade runbooks, operator wrappers) that branches on exit code 4 meaning 'shut down and recreate' now receives 4 only when the feature flag is missing and 3 for a genuine recreate requirement; a script following the previously documented contract will shut down a deployment that merely needs `--features=rolling-updates` added, and will treat a real recreate-required result (3) as an unknown/soft failure. Whoever consumes this tool's exit codes gets silently inverted semantics on upgrade.
matched_golden_ids: Need to add changelog/release notes documenting the exit code change and migration guidance
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate explicitly flags that the exit-code contract changed (renumbered/repurposed) and that this diff lacks a migration note or changelog/release notes entry, which is exactly the golden issue about documenting the exit code change and providing migration guidance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The hard feature gate breaks every pre-existing invocation of the update-compatibility commands: code that previously ran unconditionally now exits 4 with an error whenever the new preview flag is absent, and only in-tree callers (tests, docs template, operator Dockerfile) were retrofitted with the flag. Out-of-tree consumers — user upgrade scripts, CI pipelines, and any operator-side or external tooling that shells out to `kc.sh update-compatibility` from the previous release — stop working outright on upgrade, failing with exit 4 'feature not enabled' until someone discovers the flag in the docs. A PR nominally 'adding a feature flag' silently disables an existing (preview) command for all current users; this objective change should be an explicitly accepted decision, not a side effect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a hard feature gate to both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` that exits early with an error when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is not enabled (via `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...)`, `printFeatureDisabled()`, and `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` where `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`). This does change behavior for any existing invocation that previously ran without `--features=rolling-updates`, and the diff only updates in-tree docs/tests/Dockerfile to pass the flag. However, the docs were also updated with CAUTION blocks stating the command will fail unless the feature is enabled, suggesting the change is intentional rather than an unintended defect; the review point is mainly about backward-compatibility/UX and release-impact communication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The shared updatecompatibility doc macro hardcodes `--features=rolling-updates` into every documented invocation, changing the command rendered by all includes of this template rather than only the update-compatibility guide. Any other guide or page that includes this macro now instructs readers to enable the preview rolling-updates feature even where the surrounding text never mentions it, coupling unrelated documentation to this feature's preview lifecycle; when the feature graduates or is renamed, every rendered doc page using the macro breaks at once, and users who already pass their own `--features=...` list get a second, conflicting `--features` argument in the copied command.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the shared docs macro `updatecompatibility` in `docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc` to always append `--features=rolling-updates` to the rendered command: `bin/kc.[sh|bat] update-compatibility ${parameters} --features=rolling-updates`. This is a template-level coupling that will affect every place that includes this macro, not just the specific update-compatibility guide, and it can also result in duplicated/conflicting `--features` flags if `${parameters}` already contains one. While this is primarily a documentation/template design concern (not a code correctness defect in the product), it is specific and grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The custom-image build recipe bakes `--features=rolling-updates` unconditionally into every image built from it, enabling a preview feature at image-build time independent of the deployment's declared intent. Anyone using this recipe as the template for their production custom Keycloak images gets the preview rolling-updates feature silently enabled in all derived images, including images used for non-rolling deployments; the feature's enabled/disabled state is now fixed at build time rather than controlled per-deployment via the CR `features` field this same PR documents, so the two configuration paths the PR introduces can disagree.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does unconditionally add `--features=rolling-updates` to the custom image build recipe (`operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image`: `kc.sh build ... --features=rolling-updates`). In the same PR, docs and tests also show enabling the feature per-deployment via the CR `spec.features.enabled` and via CLI `--features=rolling-updates`. Baking the feature into the image can reduce/override per-deployment intent and create two potentially divergent configuration paths (image build vs CR/CLI), but this is more of a configuration/packaging concern than a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The feature-disabled guard (check + printFeatureDisabled + picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) + return) is hand-duplicated across UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata instead of being enforced once in the shared AbstractUpdatesCommand run path, and the parent UpdateCompatibility command itself carries no gate. The next command added to this family must remember to re-copy the guard or it silently bypasses the feature gate (the exact drift the guard exists to prevent); a future change to the exit code or error message — already shown to be volatile by this diff renumbering the codes — must be edited in N+1 places, and the message string 'rolling-updates' is duplicated as a literal in both copies and the test on top of the enum key.

adjudication.rationale: Both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` contain an identical feature gate block (`if (!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)) { printFeatureDisabled(); picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED); return; }`), so the concern about hand-duplicated enforcement across sibling commands is grounded in the diff. However, the claim that the error message literal is duplicated “in both copies” is not supported: the message is centralized in `AbstractUpdatesCommand#printFeatureDisabled()` and the guard uses the enum `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` rather than repeating the feature key string. The assertion that the parent `UpdateCompatibility` command has no gate cannot be verified from this diff because that class is not shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff reassigns the documented exit-code contract: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changes from 4 to 3 while the freed code 4 is repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, so any external automation pinned to these codes now conflates 'feature disabled' with 'recreate upgrade required'. Scripts, CI jobs, or operator automation written against the previous contract (exit 4 = recreate required, anything else = compatible/failure) will, on encountering the new FEATURE_DISABLED=4, take the recreate-required branch and shut down or recreate a healthy deployment, and will encounter the new recreate code 3 as an unknown error with no documented meaning; the change is verbatim in the diff (`int RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 4;` → `int RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 3; int FEATURE_DISABLED = 4;`) with no version note, changelog entry, or migration guidance anywhere in the diff, and the operator documentation added in this same diff does not document any exit codes, so operators discover the new contract only by failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (see `CompatibilityResult.java`). That is a backward-incompatible change to exit-code semantics that external automation could depend on, and the diff does not add any documentation/migration notes about the new/changed exit codes (docs added only mention enabling `rolling-updates`, not exit-code meanings). However, from the diff alone this is not provably a functional defect in Keycloak itself—more a contract/compatibility concern for consumers of these CLI exit codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] testMissingOptionOnSave was moved onto the feature-enabled path (ENABLE_FEATURE added to @Launch) but its only assertion is the negative `cliResult.assertNoMessage("Missing required argument")`, so it passes identically whether the feature was actually applied or the new gate in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() fired and short-circuited the command. If a regression makes the gate fire despite --features=rolling-updates (or the flag is silently ignored on this subcommand path), this test still passes, giving false confidence that the enabled-path option handling was exercised; nothing in the test positively verifies the metadata command reached its validation logic (no assertMessage of the preview warning, no exit-code check).

adjudication.rationale: In UpdateCommandDistTest, testMissingOptionOnSave was changed to include ENABLE_FEATURE in @Launch, but it only asserts cliResult.assertNoMessage("Missing required argument"). With the new early-return gate in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() (checks Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ROLLING_UPDATES), then printFeatureDisabled() and picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED)), the test would still pass if the command short-circuited due to the feature being considered disabled (or if the flag were not applied), because that path also would not emit the "Missing required argument" message. The diff shows no positive assertion (e.g., preview warning, exit code, or other output) proving the validation logic was reached.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new feature gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() is never triggered by any test in the diff: the only feature-disabled test (testFeatureNotEnabled) launches {UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME} and exercises only the metadata command's gate. A regression in the check command's gate (wrong message, wrong exit code, missing early return so the check runs anyway) ships undetected; the checked test file UpdateCommandDistTest.java contains no launch of UpdateCompatibilityCheck.NAME without ENABLE_FEATURE.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds identical feature-gate logic to both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() (early return with printFeatureDisabled() and exit FEATURE_DISABLED). However, in UpdateCommandDistTest, the only “feature not enabled” coverage is testFeatureNotEnabled which launches {UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME} and therefore exercises only the metadata path. All tests that include UpdateCompatibilityCheck.NAME also include ENABLE_FEATURE (e.g., testMissingOptionOnCheck, testCompatible, testWrongVersions). So a regression specific to the check command’s gate (message/exit code/return) would not be detected by this diff’s tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message text and never asserts the exit code 4 that picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) produces — the very contract the diff documents in update-compatibility.adoc's new table row 'm|4'. Scripts and automation (including the operator-facing workflows this feature targets) branch on exit codes; a regression that keeps the message but returns 0 or 3 would pass this test while breaking every consumer that dispatches on the documented code 4.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new exit-code contract for the feature-disabled case: both UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata now call `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is not enabled, and `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` is defined as `4` (with docs updated to mention the disabled-feature outcome). In `UpdateCommandDistTest#testFeatureNotEnabled`, the test only asserts the error text and does not assert the exit code, so it would not catch a regression where the message stays the same but the exit code changes. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap, not a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] testWrongVersions exercises the recreate path (incompatible versions -> 'Rolling Upgrade is not available') but asserts no exit code, so the behavioral change of RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 in CompatibilityResult.java is verified by no test in the diff. Any regression that reverts the constant to 4 (now colliding with FEATURE_DISABLED) or returns a different code on the recreate path passes the suite while silently changing the public CLI contract that external automation and the documented table row 'm|3' depend on.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the public CLI exit codes in `CompatibilityResult` (`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`). In `UpdateCommandDistTest.testWrongVersions`, the recreate path is exercised (it asserts the "[Versions] Rolling Upgrade is not available" error), but the test never asserts `result.exitCode()`. Similarly, the new `testFeatureNotEnabled` asserts only the error message, not that the exit code is 4. Therefore, the behavioral/contract change of exit codes (and avoidance of collision with FEATURE_DISABLED) is not verified by any test in the shown diff, so a regression in these constants/returned codes could pass the suite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff adds the documented claim that the Operator 'will fail' when rolling-updates is not enabled (advanced-configuration.adoc CAUTION block), but the only operator test change (createInitialDeployment) unconditionally enables the feature via FeatureSpec, and no test in the diff deploys an update strategy without it. The operator-side gating failure mode announced to users in this diff's docs is unverified: a regression that lets the operator proceed silently without the feature, or fails with an unusable error, passes the suite; scanned test files: UpgradeTest.java (the only operator test modified) references ROLLING_UPDATES only in createInitialDeployment's enabled path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s docs assert that the Operator “will fail” unless preview feature `rolling-updates` is enabled (advanced-configuration.adoc CAUTION). However, the only operator test change shown (UpgradeTest#createInitialDeployment) now explicitly enables the feature via `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))`, and there is no added/modified operator-side test covering the “feature disabled” path. So the suite changes in this diff exercise only the enabled path and do not verify the newly documented/assumed failure mode for disabled `rolling-updates`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changes from 4 to 3 while 4 is repurposed for FEATURE_DISABLED, breaking the shipped exit-code contract that existing automation and the previous docs table rely on (4 = recreate required). Scripts/CI pipelines written against the previous release's contract that branch on exit code 4 ('shut down and recreate') will instead see 3 for a required-recreate result — an unhandled code they may treat as success and attempt a rolling upgrade across incompatible versions, risking split-brain/cache corruption mid-upgrade — while an exit of 4 (feature now disabled) triggers an unnecessary full-deployment shutdown. The change is invisible to out-of-tree consumers because no migration note or versioned exit-code mapping accompanies it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (CompatibilityResult.java). That is a backwards-incompatible change in the CLI’s exit-code contract for out-of-tree consumers that may be branching on the previous numeric value. While the docs table appears updated in this diff (update-compatibility.adoc now includes code 3 for recreate and adds code 4 for feature disabled), the finding’s core concern—breaking existing automation by repurposing exit code 4—is diff-grounded. The more severe runtime consequences described (treating 3 as success, split-brain) are speculative and not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] FEATURE_DISABLED (4) reuses the exact exit code that the previous release shipped for RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE (4), while RECREATE moves to 3, so any consumer built against the released behavior misclassifies the feature-disabled exit as a 'recreate required' verdict. A script or older operator integration that ran the pre-gate `update-compatibility check` and treated exit 4 as 'the deployment must be shut down before applying the new configuration' now receives 4 whenever the preview feature is left at its default (disabled) — the compatibility check never ran at all, yet the consumer acts on it as if the check had determined a recreate is required, triggering an unnecessary full shutdown/recreate instead of either an error or a valid rolling-upgrade verdict; symmetrically, recreate verdicts that previously surfaced as 4 now arrive as 3 and land in any legacy 'unknown exit code' branch. The deliberate renumbering is documented in the comment, but the collision with the shipped value has no migration note.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (`CompatibilityResult.java`). The CLI commands now early-exit with `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `rolling-updates` is not enabled (`UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`), meaning exit code 4 no longer indicates “recreate required” as it did previously. This is a verifiable backward-incompatible behavioral change for any consumer that mapped exit code 4 to the recreate verdict, and the collision with the previously shipped meaning is exactly as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The feature gate is a copy-pasted 5-line block duplicated in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() instead of a single guard in AbstractUpdatesCommand, so the gate's coverage depends on each subcommand author remembering to paste it. The next subcommand added to UpdateCompatibility (or a refactor that reorders one of these run() methods) silently bypasses the gate and executes preview compatibility logic with the feature disabled — exactly the unguarded-execution state the docs caution causes the Operator to fail — with no compile-time or structural signal that the gate was omitted. A shared guard in AbstractUpdatesCommand.run() (or a picocli-ordering hook) would make the omission impossible rather than remembered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the same feature-enabled guard block added in both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` (`if (!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)) { ... picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED); return; }`). `AbstractUpdatesCommand` only adds `printFeatureDisabled()` but does not centralize the guard, so enforcement currently relies on each subcommand implementing the check. This is a concrete maintainability/coverage risk introduced by the change, not a present functional defect in the shown subcommands.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new caution states unqualified that 'the {project_name} Operator will fail' when the rolling-updates feature is not enabled, implying the gate applies to all update strategies including Recreate, and the updated UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment indeed sets the feature unconditionally for both Recreate and Rolling strategies. If the operator enforces the gate regardless of strategy (as the unqualified doc wording and the strategy-agnostic test setup indicate), every existing deployment running `strategy: Recreate` — which never needed a compatibility check — starts failing reconciliation after upgrading to this operator version unless the user hand-edits the CR to enable a preview feature; if the gate is actually scoped to rolling updates only, the caution overstates the failure and misdirects Recreate users into enabling an unnecessary preview feature. Either way the doc as written does not tell Recreate users what actually happens to them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds unqualified cautions stating the operator/commands will fail unless `rolling-updates` is enabled (docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc and docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc), without distinguishing update strategies. Also, the updated test helper `UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment(UpdateStrategy)` enables the `ROLLING_UPDATES` feature regardless of whether `updateStrategy` is `Recreate` or `Rolling` (it unconditionally sets `featureSpec.enabledFeatures`). However, the diff does not show operator reconciliation logic, so the claim that existing `Recreate` deployments will start failing reconciliation cannot be verified from this diff; the actionable, verifiable issue is that the docs/tests now treat the feature as universally required without clarifying scope.
